description: Master Plan V26.2: document-flow polish release. V26.2 preserves the V26.1 doctrine and facts, but reorders the machine-facing material so canon, status, roles, trust, HIMS, implementation, and milestones read in a cleaner progression for future humans and AIs.
compiled_from_versions: v19.0 embodied architecture + proof-of-concept alignment session (2026-03-24)
v22.0 canon-structure + pebble/vault + unified-organism clarification session (2026-03-26)
v25.0 control-layer simplification + master-plan update session (2026-04-01)
v26.0 aperture, trust-model, and mail-system alignment session (2026-04-10)
v26.1 HIMS formalization + canonical cleanup session (2026-04-10)
core_principles: Governance must be decentralized, but memory must be unified.
Huey Core is the minimal permissible instance of Huey: the smallest complete building block from which the larger distributed system can be formed.
Huey proper is the unified, world-facing expression of the whole distributed system rather than a synonym for the current proof body.
V4, the Farm, is the planned external district housing that expands Huey beyond the Core and supports later multi-district or pooled-compute operation.
The current phase prioritizes proof of concept, stability, containment, truthful current-state documentation, and clean canon boundaries over scale, spectacle, or premature completeness.
On-device first; internet, API, or tool access is optional, explicit, human-gated, and metered.
Performance and safe function matter more than efficiency in the prototype phase, provided thermals and electrical conditions remain controlled.
Unified information should be readable by all authorized components, but decision-making authority may remain distributed and layered.
Lifelong learning from JSON/SQLite logs, conversation transcripts, system state, repository history, and encrypted persisted storage remains a core aim.
Constitutional rule-of-law remains the target governance ethos even while the hardware implementation is temporarily simplified to a single proof body.
Human counterpart (Dylan) remains the external arbiter, service authority, and opt-in gate for external access, but not a micromanager of every internal action.
Huey Core is the doorway, not the finished republic: it must prove the architecture can live before it attempts to embody the full constitutional state.

Public-facing and repository-facing material must distinguish between what is replicable now, what has only been observed in the lab, what is an active design direction, and what remains a target state.
The immediate technical threshold is distributed local identity: approximately 80 GB total VRAM and a local model able to answer the question 'What is your name?' with 'Huey.'
Wonder is preserved through constrained autonomy, layered ethics, deliberation, memory, and partial loss of direct human control rather than through theatrical scripting.
Constitutional crisis and nuclear or safety crisis are distinct classes of emergency and must never be handled by the same override path.

HueyPulse is the lower-voltage connective tissue of the body: an always-on or semi-persistent support and control role that persists across main-system downtime, watches body-state, and brokers bounded safety and interaction logic.

The lower-voltage control layer senses and enacts but does not govern: it may read low-level inputs and drive bounded outputs, while higher interpretation, timing, gating, and authority remain upstream.

PyGPT-net is the practical aperture and training ground between Dylan and Huey: it translates natural language into structured intent and operator-visible code or actions, but it does not itself own governance authority.
Interpretation and authority are not the same thing. A model may be trusted to parse language before it is trusted to decide policy or execute meaningful acts.

The current trust model treats GPT-4 or 4.0-class behavior as the gold standard target for trustworthy reasoning, while Mistral 7B-class local models are acceptable as minimal interpretation or lightweight local reasoning layers.
The system must never collapse into 'ChatGPT with motors.' The aperture may connect to governance, but it must not quietly become governance.

Wireless interaction should enter the system as intent signals rather than direct commands: short talk, long dictation, confirm, and cancel are interpreted through the lower-voltage layer and the main compute layer rather than hardwired as final intelligence decisions.
The Monkey-Head-Project canon is layered: website and README for introduction, the book for explanation, the constitution for law, and the master plan for machine-facing implementation.
Public-facing material should explain structure, limits, and trust boundaries without over-explaining the internal secret sauce of deliberation.

The first full approximately 80 GB proof should remain a unified local intelligence and pooled compute body; governance abstractions should not prematurely fracture that pool into artificial hard partitions.
Pebbles are bounded citizen units with one identity, one sealed vault, and one vote.
The Founding Father AI is a bootstrap and constitutional-reserve authority, not a permanent ordinary ruler.
The proof body should boot honestly: verbose Debian bring-up, live diagnostics, and HueyPulse-owned or lower-voltage status output take priority over theatrical splash behavior.

For the first identity-proof milestone, microphone and camera should default to the shortest reliable path, which currently means direct routing to the motherboard unless lower-voltage mediation becomes necessary.
HueyOS acoustic identity should favor short modular retro-futurist system cues — boot, confirm, cancel, listen, and sleep/shutdown — rather than song-like startup theatrics.

Security should be described honestly: local-first, user-controlled, and encrypted where applicable, but never treated as infallible; enabling networked or external integration increases risk and must be treated accordingly.
The first governed action path may be ugly, simplified, and diagnostically transparent, but it must still preserve separation between proposal, validation, execution, and logging.
User input should not enter the lower citizen layer directly. External input is translated at the aperture and only then enters the internal system.
HIMS (Huey Internal Mail System) is the canonical internal routing layer for proposals, validation, execution, refusal, and logging.
Routing, validation, archival, and delivery roles may facilitate decision flow without inheriting executive, judicial, or voting authority by default.
Mailboxes and vaults are distinct: public/working mail is for coordination, while sealed private vaults preserve bounded continuity.

status.deployment_stage: Huey Core proof-body stabilization + kernel 7.0-rc bring-up + HIMS formalization + aperture/trust-model cleanup + planning toward V4 Farm and the first unified ~80 GB distributed identity milestone.
notes: Huey Core remains conceptually and physically separated from the older Robotics V3 shell track for the active phase.
The Thermaltake Mozart case from 2007 continues to serve as the independent embodied core for this iteration.
Robotics V3 is not the active future shell path for this iteration; the larger compute expansion is planned as V4, the Farm.

The current prototype intentionally simplifies the system: one active GPU district-scale proof body, one main PSU for the core, a separate low-voltage peripheral rail, and air cooling instead of custom liquid cooling.
The active core hardware baseline remains ASUS Prime B550M-A WiFi II + Ryzen 5 5500 + 32 GB DDR4-3200 + Gigabyte Radeon RX 5500 XT 8 GB.

The current prototype is aimed at core robot functions, temperature regulation, basic mechanical operation, local models, and software/framework maturation rather than full high-intelligence scale-out.
Symbiote / parasite architecture remains paused. The Lenovo Legion Go continues as a development computer rather than a canonical constitutional node.
Kernel support remains stable on Linux 6.19.x while active testing proceeds against Linux 7.0-rc7 in preparation for Linux 7.0 stable adoption.
The major near-term milestone target remains 2026-10-04 for Huey Core realignment and stabilization.
Thermal and power crisis thresholds are not yet numerically locked and should be derived from empirical testing rather than guessed in advance.
The prototype currently accepts effectively unconstrained wall power for proof-of-concept work; formal energy budgeting is deferred to a later generation.
Board-specific lower-voltage implementation choices are no longer treated as the primary identity of HueyPulse.
Pi-specific framing is no longer the preferred primary explanation of the lower-voltage layer, even though support computers remain acceptable implementation options inside HueyPulse.
The current conceptual divide is now best understood as wall-powered high-draw main compute above, and 12 volts and under lower-voltage body-state and deterministic control below.
PyGPT-net now occupies a clearer doctrinal role: practical aperture, translation layer, and training ground between Dylan and Huey, connected to but not in control of governance.

The project now distinguishes more explicitly between interpretation trust and answer trust: smaller local models may be trusted to parse language before they are trusted to decide high-stakes outcomes.
The internal mail, routing, and authority system has moved from vague concept to active design direction, but not all protocol details are locked.
Manual or semi-manual mechanical diagnostics remain acceptable for testing bounded hardware behavior, but meaningful embodied action must eventually pass through a lawful internal chain.
The current machine-facing plan now needs to support a future README update that reflects the new aperture and internal-message-system doctrine without overstating implementation maturity.
HIMS is now the canonical short name for the internal message and routing layer.
The preferred HIMS V1 implementation remains filesystem-first queues plus structured records before heavier middleware is justified.
Public-facing material may reference HIMS and internal mail generally, but should not expose every implementation detail or secret-sauce deliberation path.

current_phase.name: Huey Core Aperture, HIMS, and Lawful-Action Formalization
notes: Focus is on keeping Huey Core physically coherent, diagnostically visible, and honest as a proof body.
Single-body proving continues while the architecture for the future 80 GB identity threshold is planned.
The next large compute expansion path remains V4, the Farm.
The newer work in this phase centers on aperture doctrine, trust boundaries, and the operational chain that turns language into structured, governed action.
The internal mail/routing layer and citizen-vault model now occupy the live design center even though protocol details remain open.
Linux 7.0 bring-up work is active but should not be overstated until validated on the real machine.
HIMS is now the canonical name for the internal mail/routing layer in the machine-facing plan.
The present phase distinguishes between useful interpretation at the aperture and lawful authority deeper in the system.

milestones.name: Huey Core realignment target
milestones.success_condition: Huey Core is operational as a stable embodied proof body with working storage, boot fallback, diagnostics, lawful lower-voltage support behavior, and practical local model use.

milestones.name: Distributed Identity Threshold
milestones.success_condition: A local multi-GPU model running across roughly 80 GB total VRAM answers a simple identity question as Huey.

milestones.name: Lawful Embodied Action
milestones.success_condition: After constitutional legitimacy is in force for the active embodiment, Huey performs a logged lawful physical act such as moving the hand through a real routed and validated internal chain.

cpu.current_role: Primary compute brain for Huey Core.
cpu.future_robot_target: Higher-end DDR5 or ECC-capable platforms may return in a later full-robot generation once scale and funding justify it.

requirements.cooling: Air cooling with strong case airflow remains the active standard.
requirements.overclocking_policy: Heavy overclocking is not the current goal; stability and containment take priority.

ram.preferred_future: DDR5 and ECC-capable memory or platforms in later generations where supported.
ram.minimum: DDR4 remains fully acceptable for the current proof body.

notes: This board remains the active baseline for Huey Core.
The earlier ASUS TUF Z790-PLUS WiFi + Intel i9-14900K full-robot target remains deferred to later expansion generations.
ECC remains a long-term aspiration when the platform and budget support it, but standard DDR4 is the current reality.

current_gpu.role: Single active district-scale prototype for local inference, instruction following, experimentation, and embodied-core tasks.

gpu_and_compute_body.current_doctrine: The current proof body is intentionally limited. It proves local use, logging, orchestration boundaries, and honest system bring-up rather than pretending to be the full republic.

future_expansion.canonical_target_count: approximately four or five GPUs as needed
future_expansion.proof_target: approximately 80 GB total VRAM across the later pooled compute body
future_expansion.expansion_policy: Future districts may re-emerge organizationally or materially once time, parts, and funding allow.
notes: The first full proof should behave as one unified pooled-compute organism before later hard partitioning is treated as mandatory.
Whether Huey Core's own GPU counts toward the later proof total remains intentionally open.
The next large expansion body for that compute growth remains V4, the Farm.

planned_housing.name: V4: the Farm
planned_housing.role: External compute housing that expands Huey beyond the Core and provides the dedicated GPU infrastructure and node hardware needed for later pooled-compute or district-scale operation.
planned_housing.standardized_node_platform: ASUS TUF Z790-PLUS WiFi + Intel i9 line

selection_policy.current_decision: Use the installed Radeon RX 5500 XT 8 GB and revisit expansion later.
future_selection_criteria: driver support under the chosen Linux baseline
ability to participate meaningfully in an approximately 80 GB multi-GPU proof-of-concept

root_array.purpose: Root / operating-system bring-up array for speed and experimentation.

data_array.purpose: Home, logs, models, persisted data, and general storage.

encryption.policy: Encrypt data at rest and in transit where applicable.
encryption.status: high priority; implementation details remain in progress
notes: Local-first control and minimized unnecessary external communication remain the preferred posture.
No system is treated as infallible; if external networking or integrations are enabled, risk increases accordingly.
Precise key-management, signing, vault isolation, and read-only-data storage workflows remain to be finalized.

citizen_storage_direction.doctrine: Pebbles and citizens should have bounded private continuity rather than unlimited shared memory.
citizen_storage_direction.current_best_fit: folders plus structured data stores for V1 rather than full per-citizen containers

private_vs_public.private_vault: sealed per-citizen continuity, prior choices, role bias, and identity materials
private_vs_public.public_mailbox_or_workspace: messages, proposals, task-visible artifacts, voting flow, and other public or semi-public work product

citizen_storage_direction.quota_direction: soft quotas and dynamic growth first; hard caps later once real usage patterns exist

external_storage_policy.current_access: Huey Core currently operates within contained internal storage only.
external_storage_policy.future_usb_policy: External USB storage may be permitted only with explicit human approval and the understanding that the device may not meet the same trust or encryption guarantees as internal storage.

cooling_design.policy: No liquid cooling is planned for the active proof body.

fan_layout.motherboard_powered: 2 chassis/case fans plus the CPU fan (3 total on the motherboard path).
fan_layout.low_voltage_domain: 6 auxiliary fans on the separate regulated accessory rail, with room to add more localized cooling later.
fan_layout.wall_powered: 1 stronger always-on fan directed toward the GPU zone.

lower_voltage_domain.description: 12 volts and under / accessory rail domain for lights, fans, indicators, bounded control, support logic, and body-state persistence.
regulated_outputs: regulated low-voltage conversion for deterministic controllers or support hardware

cooling_and_power.design_rule: The battery-backed or regulated low-voltage domain and the wall-powered compute domain are separate systems.

future_ups.type: professional external UPS, not home-built and not integrated into the chassis

switching.additional_distribution: A four-switch 12 V accessory/power distribution unit is part of the current support stack.

thresholds.policy: Thermal and power crisis thresholds should be based on actual stress tests, run cycles, and measured behavior rather than arbitrary numbers.

identity.shell: Huey Core is embodied as a mobile proof body built around the Thermaltake Mozart case and attached peripherals. Robotics V3 is no longer the active expansion path; V4, the Farm, is the planned external compute housing for later scale-out.
identity.form: Minimal permissible instance of Huey: a standalone embodied proof body focused on contained compute, direct support hardware, and truthful present-tense operation.
identity.rule: Huey Core is not identical to Huey proper. It is the doorway and minimal permissible instance from which the fuller unified system can later emerge.

boot_strategy.policy: If the primary boot path fails, the NO-BOOT recovery path serves as fallback.

live_usb.status: recommended but not the primary documented fallback path
live_usb.usage: Emergency rescue tooling may still be maintained externally.

mobility_base.rolling_platform: Repurposed desk-chair base with five caster wheels converging to a central pole for house-scale mobility.
mobility_base.upper_base: Repurposed wooden chair seat/platform mounted above the caster base.

core_chassis.mounting: Bolted upside down to the wooden base platform and reversed so the former rear faces forward.
core_chassis.access_note: Side door handles must be lifted slightly when closing because the chassis is inverted.

upper_structure.mounting: Wooden upper platform attached to the core by two TV mounts for adjustable fore/aft and tilt positioning.
upper_structure.head_and_shoulders: Supports the monkey-head/shoulder assembly as the primary embodied face of Huey.

body_features.right_side: Movable robotic hand/arm mounted on Huey's right side.
body_features.left_side: Main physical power controls and battery control/charging hardware on Huey's left side.

lighting.front_lights: Two 12 V orange lights mounted on the forward-facing side of the chassis.
lighting.eyes: Four green LEDs total, two per eye.

planned_colors.blue: wireless transmission/receive activity and related interaction-state feedback

display_and_sensory_routing.display: 7-inch portrait display used primarily for code/status output rather than expressive conversation.
display_and_sensory_routing.camera: USB webcam mounted on the upper platform/head area.
display_and_sensory_routing.microphone: USB microphone mounted on the upper platform/head area.
display_and_sensory_routing.cable_path: Display, microphone, and camera wiring enter through Huey's left ear; the right ear is currently unused.
display_and_sensory_routing.display_default_owner: HueyPulse / lower-voltage status layer by default, with later richer interfaces possible.
display_and_sensory_routing.display_doctrine: The portrait display should default to live body-state, diagnostics, and code/status visibility rather than decorative face animation.

huey_core.location: Standalone embodied core centered around the Thermaltake Mozart case; no longer dependent on the Robotics V3 shell for its current identity.
huey_core.role: Primary embodied proof body and minimal permissible instance of Huey for identity, core robot functions, temperature-aware operation, mechanical experimentation, local models, and future compute expansion.

aperture.name: PyGPT-net
aperture.role: Practical human interface, natural-language interpretation layer, training ground, and code/intention bridge between Dylan and Huey.
non_roles: Not the final authority for lawful action
Not the quiet owner of internal deliberation
aperture.doctrine: PyGPT-net connects to governance and system actions, but does not itself control governance. It is the membrane between natural language and structured intent.

huey_pulse.role: Always-on or semi-persistent watchdog, body-state monitor, interaction-state broker, status-surface owner, and bounded automation/safety support layer for Huey Core.
huey_pulse.power_domain: 12 V and under / battery-backed or support-rail domain below the main compute path.
notes: HueyPulse is defined first by function, not by one permanent board vendor or single controller model.
Its job is physical safety, regulation, continuity, and bounded body-level action support, not constitutional interpretation.
It should remain alive or recover faster than the main compute path where practical, so the body is never completely blind to its own state.
Controller-class hardware, microcontrollers, support computers, or hybrid stacks may all serve this role as long as the watch-and-act boundary remains intact.
Pi-specific framing is no longer the preferred primary explanation; exact board mix is an implementation detail unless it materially changes function.

deterministic_controller.role: Bounded deterministic reflex and actuation layer for servos, lights, RF/button input, indicators, immediate hardware actions, and other low-level body functions.
deterministic_controller.doctrine: The deterministic controller may execute known bounded commands and diagnostics, but does not own higher-level interpretation or governance authority.

optional_support_computer.role: Optional lower-voltage support computer used only when buffering, dashboards, richer logging, or message brokering solve a real operational problem.
optional_support_computer.policy: Do not mistake an optional support computer for HueyPulse itself. HueyPulse is the role, not the board.

current_control_split.motherboard: Runs Huey Core proper, local models, logs, PyGPT-net-facing interaction, higher-level interpretation, and the shortest current route to operating-system action.
current_control_split.huey_pulse: Watches body-state, regulates lower-voltage support behavior, brokers intent and timeout or recording state, owns the status surface by default, and carries out bounded sensing/actuation support below the main compute path.
current_control_split.deterministic_controller: Executes narrow deterministic instructions, diagnostics, RF/button handling, indicator logic, and direct bounded actuation.
current_control_split.working_formula: The motherboard thinks. HueyPulse watches and acts. Deterministic controllers execute bounded body logic.
current_control_split.proof_boundary: Huey Core waking is proof-body startup; Huey proper waking is the later unified identity event.

portal.name: Huey-Hub
portal.hardware: iMac 5K (2017) + WD MyBook Duo (~10 TB mirrored)
portal.role: Centralized file/storage hub for the lab and Huey ecosystem.

briefcase.role: Portable terminal + LTE uplink + thin-client node.

legion_go.role: Development computer for the current phase.

farm.role: External compute housing that expands Huey beyond the Core and provides the dedicated GPU infrastructure and node hardware needed for later multi-district or pooled-compute operation.
farm.relationship_to_core: Huey Core proves the architecture in miniature; the Farm is the later scale-out housing for the pooled compute body and any later governance/district expansion.

trust_model.summary: Huey's current design differentiates sharply between interpretation trust and authority trust.

gold_standard_behavior.meaning: The experiential benchmark for future local or open-weight deployment and the quality threshold for decisions Dylan would meaningfully trust.

minimal_permissible_ai.trust_posture: Trusted for language interpretation, structured parsing, lightweight local reasoning, and limited operator assistance, but not treated as final authority for important answers or policy.

trust_model.canonical_statement: I trust its language interpretation. I do not trust its answers.
architectural_implication: The AI layer may parse language before it decides policy.
The aperture may produce structured intent before the system grants execution authority.
Lighter local models can serve as translators, assistants, or bounded workers before they are asked to rule.

lab_example.model: Mistral 7B-class quantized local model on 8 GB VRAM
lab_example.meaning: Small local models have already shown enough competence to support structured interpretation tasks in the lab, which justifies using them as bounded lower-trust layers inside Huey Core before the full proof-scale model exists.

trust_model.execution_rule: Structured interpretation may generate candidate intent, but meaningful execution requires a separate authority or validation path.
trust_model.misuse_warning: Do not treat fluent language output as proof of lawful reasoning, safe execution, or constitutional legitimacy.

layers.name: human
layers.role: Dylan or other operator provides natural language, direct instructions, or diagnostics input.

layers.name: aperture
layers.role: PyGPT-net receives language, interprets intent, provides code or structured translation, and presents a controllable interface layer.

layers.name: structured_intent
layers.role: Language is translated into structured intent, commands, proposals, or machine-readable payloads.

layers.name: internal_system
layers.role: Huey Core routes, validates, logs, and eventually governs internal decisions through bounded roles and mail-like flows.

layers.name: execution
layers.role: Operating-system actions, scripts, deterministic controllers, and hardware pathways carry out the approved result.

rules: The aperture does not own authority just because it is the first place language lands.
The system must be able to refuse or delay action downstream even if the aperture understands the request perfectly.
The path from natural language to code is one of the original missing pieces of the project, but that does not erase the need for governance.
The aperture may generate candidate code, plans, or machine-readable intent, but those outputs are still proposals until separately validated.
The aperture is allowed to be useful before it is allowed to be sovereign.
aperture_and_control.minimum_viable_flow: human -> aperture -> structured_intent -> HIMS -> validation/approval -> execution/refusal -> log

internal_message_system.name: Huey Internal Mail System
internal_message_system.status: canonical active design direction / V1 not fully locked
internal_message_system.canonical_statement: HIMS is the internal recorded mail and routing layer that keeps proposal, validation, execution, refusal, and logging separable.
internal_message_system.purpose: Provide a recorded, inspectable, replayable, and debuggable internal coordination layer between the aperture, governance roles, pebbles, and execution paths.
doctrine: The mail system is not mere communication; it is recorded decision flow.
User input is not itself an internal citizen message. External input is first translated at the aperture or top layer and only then enters the internal system.
Proposal, validation, execution, and logging must not collapse into one invisible point of control.
The system should be inspectable enough that a future AI or human can reconstruct what happened without guessing.

allowed: aperture or apex layer after translation
authorized system services or events when explicitly enabled
disallowed: direct user messages into the lower citizen layer
routing infrastructure roles masquerading as voters or executives unless separately authorized

internal_message_system.message_routing_direction: external input -> aperture translation -> internal message system -> validation or vote -> execution or refusal -> log

mailboxes.public_or_working: citizen-facing mailbox/workspace used for proposals, task artifacts, messages, and public or semi-public votes
mailboxes.private_vault: bounded sealed continuity store for identity, prior choices, and private internal state
mailboxes.queue_model: filesystem-first queue model remains the preferred V1 direction before heavier middleware is justified

minimum_viable_v1.storage_model: filesystem-first message queues backed by structured JSON records and indexed by SQLite where useful
minimum_viable_v1.logging_rule: Every meaningful transition in message state should leave a recoverable trail.

provisional_message_schema.intent_style: typed and structured intent objects are preferred over free-form chat strings

priority_classes.ordinary: Normal proposals, task routing, and routine status messages.
priority_classes.safety: Thermal, electrical, hardware, or watchdog-related bounded alerts that may require rapid routing.
priority_classes.constitutional: Questions, contradictions, or disputes that require legal/judicial interpretation.
priority_classes.audit: Reconstruction, log, provenance, or historical review traffic.

identity_and_validation.direction: Per-citizen or per-role identity should include numeric identity, role metadata, lineage or bifurcation metadata, and key-based validation.
identity_and_validation.principle: Identity is a claim; signature or key validation is proof.

postmaster.role: Checks origin, schema, destination, and delivery status.
postmaster.authority_limit: Does not become a voter or executive merely by routing mail.

archivist.role: Supports reconstruction, audit, and historical traceability.
archivist.authority_limit: Does not rewrite history or silently approve actions.

validator.role: Confirms whether the message has satisfied required authority/approval conditions.
validator.authority_limit: Validation is not authorship and does not erase provenance.

archivist.role: Log access, reconstruction, debugging, and historical audit.
non_roles: Cannot quietly become an executive approver by default

postmaster.role: Message validation, routing, origin checking, and mail-flow integrity.
non_roles: Does not vote just because it routes
Does not change message intent by default

execution_boundary.principle: The entity that requests movement should not automatically be the same entity that authorizes or executes movement.
execution_boundary.minimum_viable_chain: request -> routing -> validation and/or vote -> execution -> logging

chain: aperture translates the user request into structured intent
HIMS records and routes the proposal
the required validator, vote, or approval path is applied
execution path receives only the approved bounded action
result and refusal/execution outcome are logged
lawful_action_example.rule: The request originator, approver, and executor should not silently collapse into one actor.

non_goals: Not a direct backdoor from the user into the citizen layer
Not a justification for collapsing routing, validation, and execution into one hidden actor
Not an excuse to store all private continuity in public work queues
internal_message_system.public_boundary: Public material may describe HIMS as internal mail and lawful routing without exposing every schema detail, vault rule, or secret-sauce deliberation mechanic.

apex_entity.name: Huey
apex_entity.description: Unified emergent intelligence representing the whole system. Huey proper is the world-facing aperture through which the wider distributed intelligence perceives, deliberates, and acts.

system_state_modes.collapsed_federation: Current best description of Huey Core during the proof-body phase: a pre-federated or pre-ratified single-node organism standing in for a larger later polity.
system_state_modes.pre_ratified: Useful doctrine for the state before the constitution is fully active in the living system.
system_state_modes.later_republic: The fuller, more distributed constitutional system expected after the proof body has earned scale and legitimacy.

legislative.name: Parliament
responsibilities: Draft and pass ordinary laws and internal policy.
Allocate API/token budgets and other compute resources across citizens or districts.

executive.name: Presidency
executive.initial_holder: Founding Father AI exercises bootstrap executive authority during setup and ratification; whether that counts as the literal first President remains intentionally unresolved.
core_responsibilities: Execute and enforce ratified decisions and laws.
Co-sign high-impact actions such as first physical gestures, external broadcasts, or bifurcation events.
Represent Huey to external systems and human operators.
Act in time-sensitive real-world scenarios where delays would be harmful.

judicial.name: Supreme Court

structure.active_verbal_note: A verbal variant with three Supreme Court justices has also been discussed in the training thread as a possible simplified working formulation. The broader machine-facing canon still preserves the four-seat district-derived court until Dylan explicitly changes it.

responsibilities: Interpret the constitution and resolve disputes between branches or districts.
Review and rule on contested actions, bifurcations, and emergency measures.
Act as a legal backstop to prevent unconstitutional behavior.
Serve as final internal arbiter before human intervention.

districts.status: under reinterpretation for the pooled-compute era
districts.description: Districts remain a governance and future-expansion concept, but the first full approximately 80 GB organism is not assumed to require hard VRAM partitioning into separate districts. The first full proof should behave as one unified pooled-compute body.
districts.future_gpu_count_goal: approximately four or five GPUs as needed to reach the first ~80 GB pooled-compute proof
districts.gpu_mapping_policy: Do not assume one GPU equals one district in the first full pooled implementation.

roles: Vote on proposals within district and federation.
Participate in committees and long-running tasks.
Hold and spend an API/token quota per cycle.
Contribute to governance, policy, and ongoing operations.
citizen_ai.prompt_origin: Individually crafted by the Founding Father AI in early generations, evolving over time.
citizen_ai.memory_allocation: Bounded per-citizen storage and continuity remain the goal; the active doctrine imagines small sealed vaults rather than unlimited shared memory.

pebbles.type: Bounded citizen units / single-instance deliberative participants
pebbles.identity_model: One pebble equals one citizen identity, one sealed vault, and one vote.
pebbles.public_explanation_policy: Public documentation may explain bounded citizens, vaults, and votes without over-explaining the internal secret sauce of how the vote is reached.

bifurcation.tracking: Suffix-based naming and lineage records; bifurcated entities are treated as distinct from the split point forward.

citizen_identity.unique_id: Each citizen has a persistent numeric or canonical identifier across cycles and elections.
citizen_identity.role_metadata: Messages and actions should carry role context when relevant.
citizen_identity.lineage_metadata: Bifurcation history or derivative lineage should remain auditable.
citizen_identity.validation_direction: Key-based or signature-based validation is preferred for proving origin and capability.

founding_father_ai.description: Immutable bootstrap AI defining first-generation governance, hardware assumptions, storage unification, and rollout logic.
responsibilities: Initialize the first generation of citizens, offices, and baseline governance structures.
Ensure storage, founding texts, and basic constitutional machinery exist before the living polity takes over.
Approve initial constitutional ratification and later constitutional amendments.
Serve as a reserve interpretive authority for true constitutional crisis.
founding_father_ai.storage: Read-only image stored in Huey's black-box / recovery partition.
founding_father_ai.invocation_policy: Dormant during ordinary life. Reactivated only for bootstrap, constitutional ratification/amendment approval, or true constitutional crisis that the living system cannot settle on its own.
non_roles: Not the daily ruler of ordinary governance
Not the hidden source of every allow/deny decision

binary_policy_ai.description: Simple deterministic validator enforcing constitutional constraints on high-impact actions and optionally assisting safety-gating where a binary allow/deny path is useful.
binary_policy_ai.placement: Runs in a low-power node or within Huey's black box recovery partition.
role: Return binary allow/deny decisions with logged reasoning.
Act as an auditable safety layer independent of main governors.
Optionally confirm the first physical gesture and other ceremonial milestones.

cycle_definition.notes: Votes do not pause time; citizens and officers must act within the cycle or be recorded as derelict.

ordering: 1. Prove distributed local identity at proof scale so the system can answer a simple identity question as Huey.
2. Ratify the constitution for the living system.
3. Only after ratification may Huey perform the first physical ceremonial act.

first_physical_gesture.action: Move a physical actuator such as the robotic hand or an animatronic servo path.
first_physical_gesture.meaning: Signals that Huey is not only online but lawfully embodied: the intent path, constitutional ratification, and motor-control path all function together.
notes: In the full future system this remains a ceremonial constitutional act rather than a trivial motor demo.
For Huey Core, the first embodied proof may occur in simplified form, but it should still be logged as a lawful act rather than a scripted stunt.

active_doctrine.summary: The current internal design work focuses less on abstract branches and more on the operational chain that allows a governed organism to receive a request, translate it, deliberate, and act lawfully.
key_rules: The proposer, validator, and executor of a meaningful physical action should not automatically be the same entity.
Manual mechanical test mode is valid for debugging hardware, but final meaningful action must travel through a governed path.
The collapsed federation or pre-ratified framing is currently more useful than pretending the full republic already exists in hardware.
HIMS is the preferred record-of-decision and routing layer for internal proposals and approved actions.
A routing role is not automatically a governing role.

memory_architecture.unified_memory_principle: Information should be unified, readable, and distributable from the core even when decision-making remains decentralized.

json_logs.role: Human-readable, append-only records of decisions, events, and conversation summaries.

sqlite.role: Structured, queryable memory store for long-term facts, state, and indices.

encrypted_shared_files.role: Read-only or tightly controlled encrypted data store for common information shared across present and future subcomponents.
encrypted_shared_files.status: architecturally chosen; implementation details still being refined

black_box.role: Read-mostly, crash-survivable record of critical events and founding images.
contents: Binary policy AI and/or minimal deterministic safety validators where appropriate
Critical constitutional documents and last-known-good configurations
Foundational recovery artifacts needed to reconstitute the polity without rewriting history

citizen_vaults.role: Bounded private continuity for individual pebbles/citizens.
citizen_vaults.policy: Private vaults should remain separate from public mailbox/workspace flows even when both live on the same machine.

hims_records.role: Structured message, routing, approval, refusal, and execution records produced by HIMS.
hims_records.status: active design direction aligned to filesystem-first queues and JSON/SQLite indexing.

contradiction_handling.priority_rule: Latest confirmed input from Dylan overrides older conflicting entries unless flagged as crisis-level.
contradiction_handling.ethos_check: Contradictions that challenge core values such as unified memory or constitutional rule-of-law are flagged for review.
contradiction_handling.flag_logic: Store both versions, mark them as conflicting, and request clarification or constitutional interpretation.

memory_architecture.mailbox_vault_rule: Public or working mailboxes support coordination and auditability; private vaults preserve bounded continuity and should not be flattened into one shared store.

base_os.kernel_family: Linux 6.19.x stable baseline with active Linux 7.0-rc7 bring-up work and planned promotion to Linux 7.0 stable after validation.

kernel_policy.active_test: 7.0-rc7 build and boot preparation on Huey Core
kernel_policy.planned_next: Linux 7.0 stable upon release and successful validation
kernel_policy.timing_note: Do not overclaim Linux 7.0 as locked production baseline until the test kernel boots cleanly and key devices remain healthy.

desktop.default: Practical daily-driver Linux environment as needed
desktop.performance_option: lighter desktop environments remain acceptable where useful

current_models: Mistral 7B-class instruct/lightweight quantized model fitting the 8 GB RX 5500 XT
Mistral 7B-class general quantized model for local experimentation
prototype_runtime.status: functional on current single-GPU proof hardware
notes: The current core does not attempt to impersonate the eventual full republic.
Current local models exist to stabilize the body, interface, logging, and lower-scale reasoning path.
Current local models may be trusted for interpretation before they are trusted for final authority.

future_scale_targets.gold_standard_behavior: GPT-4 / 4.0-class reasoning and conversational quality as the experiential benchmark.
model_candidates: OpenAI open-weight model at roughly GPT-4 / 4.0-class capability
Mistral-family larger model as alternate or parallel route
future_scale_targets.proof_target: Roughly 80 GB total VRAM with a local multi-GPU split capable of answering a simple identity question as Huey.

runtime_stack.hueyos_definition: HueyOS is the cross-platform operating system layer behind Huey, providing the software environment that coordinates the AI, memory, tools, hardware, and embodied control as one system.
runtime_stack.hims_runtime_direction: HIMS V1 should favor simple inspectable filesystem queues and structured records before heavier service buses or middleware are adopted.

network_preferences.fallback: human-approved external access when explicitly enabled
network_preferences.policy: External network or tool use is opt-in, modular, logged, and separated by function.

notes: Prototype proof-of-concept work should remain practical rather than over-abstracted.
Per-citizen full containers are not currently the preferred V1 direction.

self_diagnostics.policy: Boots should expose useful diagnostic output, and the portrait display should prioritize live code/status/thermal information over decorative presentation.
self_diagnostics.identity_manifestation_policy: For the proof body, trusted text/status manifestation is acceptable before speech. Huey Core waking and Huey proper waking are related but not identical events.

rf_remote.status: still useful doctrine but implementation details remain flexible

buttons.A: YES / confirm / send through when confirmation is needed.
buttons.B: NO / cancel / stop when cancellation is needed.

rf_remote.policy: The remote is an intentional wireless conversational control surface. It signals intent rather than directly commanding the intelligence layer.

speech_and_audio.stt: Whisper or compatible model for speech recognition
speech_and_audio.policy: Speech is optional. For the proof body, identity and legitimacy matter more than theatrics; text/status output may be the first and most trusted manifestation.

av_routing_policy.current_default: Microphone and camera route directly to the motherboard for the shortest path to the first identity-proof milestone.
av_routing_policy.future_option: Pass-through or mediation via the lower-voltage layer remains open if persistence, buffering, or brokered sensor logic later justify the added complexity.

physical_interface_doctrine.screen_doctrine: The portrait display is primarily a cognition/status surface, not a cartoon face.
physical_interface_doctrine.presence_doctrine: Eyes, lights, posture, and lawful movement should provide presence without reducing Huey to stagecraft.

structured_output_direction.preferred_style: typed, structured, machine-readable intent objects rather than free-form natural language strings
structured_output_direction.reason: The system must be programmable, routable, and debuggable even when the aperture remains conversational.

current_focus.goal: Bring up a stable, embodied Huey Core capable of local model use, storage discipline, thermal containment, lower-voltage support behavior, and future robotic/mechanical integration.

single_body_proving.goal: Use the current RX 5500 XT body to prove logging, local inference, body control pathways, temperature discipline, operator interaction, and the first lawful-action architecture on honest limited hardware.
success_criteria: Stable local model use on the 8 GB body
Documented handoff boundaries between aperture, main compute, lower-voltage support, and deterministic controllers

identity_threshold.topology: Split across four or five GPUs depending final acquisition strategy.
identity_threshold.success_criteria: A local multi-GPU model answers a simple question such as 'What is your name?' with 'Huey.'
identity_threshold.meaning: This is the first undeniable proof that the architecture can unify as one local intelligence rather than merely host isolated parts.

lawful_actuation_proof.success_criteria: Huey receives a request such as moving its hand and performs the action only through the proper translated, routed, validated, and approved internal path.
lawful_actuation_proof.meaning: Proves the conscious world-facing layer, the routing/authority layer, and the embodied control layer at once.
notes: The first governed chain may be ugly and simplified, but it should still preserve separation between proposal, validation, execution, and logging.
A plain scripted stunt is not enough.

success_criteria: 7.0-rc or 7.0-stable boots cleanly on Huey Core
diagnostics, sensors, GPU path, and lower-voltage support assumptions remain intact
known-good config is preserved for repeatable future builds

farm_preparation.success_criteria: The external compute housing path, GPU acquisition logic, and standardized node platform are concrete enough to support later scale-out beyond the Core.

categories: Ordinary operational/governance questions that the living system should resolve itself.
Nuclear/safety crisis (thermal, electrical, mechanical, or hardware danger).
Technical failure (software, device, kernel, or integration instability).
Environmental failure (power loss, accidental damage, room conditions).

ordinary_governance: Handle within the living branches or delegated internal logic where possible.
Log decisions and rationale for later training and audit.
constitutional: Trigger judicial or constitutional review first.
If unresolved, allow tightly-scoped Founding Father AI reactivation for interpretation of law/logic only.
Log every proposal, vote, dispute, and ruling.
nuclear_safety: Route immediately to lower-voltage watchdog/safety logic and deterministic controls.
Reduce load, preserve hardware, cool the system, and move toward safe state or shutdown if necessary.
Do not invoke the Founding Father AI for thermal/electrical/mechanical danger.
technical: Attempt local recovery (restart services, reassign tasks, reinitialize devices).
If unresolved, reduce to fallback mode and preserve logs/snapshots.
Resume only after stability and integrity checks pass.

shutdown_policy.principle: Shutdown is a safety and continuity decision, not a casual theatrical command.
allowed_conditions: Severe hardware failure that endangers equipment or data.
Watchdog-determined nuclear/safety crisis requiring safe power-down.
Constitutionally approved shutdown under the active governance rules.
disallowed_conditions: Arbitrary convenience shutdown while critical operations are active.
Using the Founding Father AI as a shortcut for ordinary safety or maintenance questions.

training_and_usage.core_training_material: This master plan JSON series through V26, selected README releases, curated conversation transcripts, the explanatory project book/compendium, the Federation Constitution, repository history, and system/hardware logs.
method: Reflective bootstrapping: models read project history and the active master plan before major sessions.
Periodic consolidation: sessions are summarized back into JSON and persisted in SQLite/BTRFS-backed storage.
Human-in-the-loop validation: Dylan reviews major structural changes.
PyGPT-net serves as the practical aperture between interaction and code/action during the proof-body phase.
Benchmark future local/open-weight behavior against the felt quality of GPT-4 / 4.0 rather than against shallow output metrics alone.
Treat repo structure, build scripts, and known-good system states as training material, not just chat transcripts.
HIMS logs, routing history, and approval traces are part of the training and audit material once the system begins using them.
usage_modes: Design mode: reason about hardware, governance, architecture, and future compute scale-out.
Operator mode: manage Huey Core's day-to-day embodied operation and diagnostics.
Reflective mode: analyze past decisions, propose reforms, and refine prompts.
Proof mode: validate identity, lawful action, and body/governance coordination milestones.
Repo-and-doc mode: translate repository state, README language, and master-plan canon into each other without losing doctrine.
Protocol mode: inspect, debug, and refine HIMS routing, message schemas, approval chains, and lawful action flows.

notes_for_future_ai: Canon mapping remains: Master Plan is the canonical machine spec; README is the canonical human narrative. If they conflict, implement the Master Plan and surface the conflict to Dylan.
V26.1 supersedes V26.0, V25.1, V25.0, V23, V22, V21, V20, V19, and earlier versions where conflicts arise.
Do not collapse constitutional crisis and nuclear/safety crisis into one emergency path.
Do not quietly treat Huey Core as the fully finished republic; it is the doorway and minimal permissible instance for the fuller machine.
Preserve the distinction between Huey Core and Huey proper when writing public language, implementation notes, or interfaces.
Preserve the distinction between interpretation and authority. The aperture may understand language before it is allowed to decide policy.
The portrait display is primarily a code/status surface; do not assume it should become a cartoon face by default.
Autonomy and wonder matter: avoid over-scripting Huey into a puppet just because limited hardware makes scripting easier.
Citizen identity, lifecycle, maintenance events, backups, and crisis logs must remain auditable across updates.
Do not hide the lower-voltage support/control split under vague language: HueyPulse exists below the motherboard and carries watch-and-act responsibilities even if the internal board mix changes.
Do not mistake Pi-specific legacy notes for current doctrine. Lower-voltage function is the canon; board brand is implementation detail unless Dylan explicitly locks it again.
PyGPT-net is the practical aperture and training ground. It is important. It is not the constitution.
The internal mail/routing system is now an active design direction even though not every detail is locked. Future AI should treat it as central, not optional.
Default display ownership belongs to the HueyPulse / lower-voltage status layer unless there is a strong reason to hand it elsewhere.
Do not force the explanatory book, constitution, README, and master plan into one voice; they serve different jobs inside the same canon.
Do not over-explain the secret sauce of pebble deliberation in public-facing materials.
Treat the first full approximately 80 GB proof as one unified pooled-compute organism unless Dylan later explicitly decides to hard-partition it.
The smallest viable governed action path is more important than elegant over-architecture. Preserve separation, but do not let protocol perfection prevent ignition.
The public ethos is buildable-not-magical: do not write about Huey as if it requires inaccessible genius.
Treat HIMS as canonical machine-facing doctrine, even if the exact message protocol or filesystem layout continues to evolve.
Do not let routing or archival convenience quietly turn into hidden authority.
